details:
- CVE-2026-84784: advance the QUIC retire-prior-to counter only when the peer
  acknowledges the RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame, as the protocol requires, so
  retire frames queued for a peer that withholds ACKs are no longer counted
  as retired and the connection ID limit check keeps applying
- CVE-2026-75805: skip the CMP revocation response CertId issuer and serial
  checks when the revoked certificate was given as a PKCS#10 CSR, so a
  server returning a CertId can no longer crash the client with a NULL
  pointer dereference
- CVE-2026-75806: reject TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 AEAD records shorter than the
  explicit IV and tag before AEAD processing, so TLS reports bad_record_mac
  and DTLS drops the record instead of raising an internal error alert
- CVE-2026-54872: pin the scalar and its padded sum to a fixed word width
  in the EC Montgomery ladder, so the scalar padding additions no longer
  leak the bit length of the secret scalar through timing
- CVE-2026-42772: replace the linear QUIC stream frame list with a red-black
  tree of stream ranges, so a peer sending many small out-of-order STREAM
  frames can no longer make the receiver spend quadratic time reassembling
  them
- CVE-2026-54873: limit the memory that buffered QUIC STREAM chunks retain in
  their received packets (the packet size beyond the chunk data) to about
  64 kB per connection by copying further chunks out of their packets, so a
  peer can no longer make the receiver hold a whole packet buffer for every
  small STREAM frame; stream data past the announced final size now closes
  the connection with FINAL_SIZE_ERROR
